alex: heads up — seeing 3x tail latency for private VPC workloads in us-west-2 started ~02:00 UTC. throughput drops, lots of retries. infra-gw CPU spiked and conntrack is near capacity :warning:
katie: when did this start? any deploys or config changes? :eyes:
alex: first spike at 01:58, small deploy at 01:50 but release looks unrelated. alert from infra-bot at 02:01 for conntrack 92%
infra-bot: ALERT conntrack_table_utilization=92% node=nat-gw-7f4a cpu=78% egress_packets_s=~120k
jamal: curious — did kernel-selector fallback happen? last week we saw fallback to generic kernel under high MTU fragmentation which killed skb_kv path and batching efficiency
maya: we ran a profiler during 02:05 — kv-cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 38%, and batching heuristics started emitting tiny batches (~1-2 requests). rough snippet from profiler logs:
```
[02:06:02] kv_cache_hits=62 kv_cache_misses=38 batching_avg_size=1.9 batching_tail_ms=48 kernel_path=generic_sg fallback=true
[02:06:12] conntrack_est=650k conntrack_max=700k nat_sessions_active=620k
```
dev-runtime: that matches: generic kernel disables optimized gather/dma scatter kernels we rely on for fast KV and causes more syscalls per token. also fragmentation due to MTU mismatch + SNAT hairpin increases per-packet overhead
katie: any firewall rule change that could cause logging noise? we had a temporary rule for a compliance scan last night
alex: yes — firewall rule 1009 had logging enabled at 00:30 for a scan. logs spiked ~01:55. looks correlated with CPU and conntrack growth. logs are being NATed and go through the same path
sre_lead: short term mitigation suggestions? increase conntrack, disable logging, adjust SNAT pool?
jamal: quick wins — 1) disable rule 1009 logging, 2) sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max += 200k (temporary), 3) reduce SNAT sticky timeout to free ephemeral ports: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300`, 4) pin kernel-selector to optimized kernel on nat-gw nodes (`/etc/kselector/pin kernel=fast-sg`), 5) bump batching latency target so runtime emits larger batches: update config `batching.max_wait_ms=40 -> 80`
maya: ran 1-3 in staging, saw conntrack utilization drop and kv-hit rate recover to ~86% in 5m. patch deployed to prod at 02:20. tail latency down to baseline by 02:32
alex: rolling change for firewall logging off and kernel pin across remaining nat-gw pool. creating follow-up ticket INF-2319 with timeline and must-fix list
katie: opened INF-2319, assigning to jamal + maya. also scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PT.
dev-runtime: we should add an alert for rapid kv-cache-miss % increase + small batching size, that would catch this earlier. filing DEVOPS-987
sre_lead: nice work triaging. blockers: coordinate with security for firewall log change; mark as mitigated for now and we will run root cause from profiling artifacts. :thumbsup: 
alex: thanks everyone — will push a short incident note to #incidents and upload profiler traces to the ticket.
